body_markdown:
Nobody gets into sales to do data entry. Sellers want to build relationships and close deals, yet the average seller[spends 60% of their time](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/state-of-sales-report-announcement-2026/) on non-selling activities like manually updating CRM systems and researching accounts. Sales leaders feel the pain, too; relying on data that reps have to enter manually leaves the critical deal context they need to forecast and manage pipelines late, untrustworthy, or missing altogether.


Sales agents are being deployed across businesses to solve these exact issues, but are they actually working?


To understand the return on investment of Salesforce Sales Cloud agents, Salesforce polled 24 customers who are active users of Sales Cloud’s AI sales agents. Today, we launched[The ROI Report: Sales Cloud Agents](http://salesforce.com/sales/resources/sales-agent-roi-report) , which delivers some key findings from customers.


The data shows that, by taking on administrative tasks across the sales cycle,[Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/cloud/?d=cta-body-promo-8) agents save reps an average of six hours per week to refocus on actually selling. Simultaneously, agents improve pipeline visibility and deal context: 63% of customers report that sales agents give them more accurate and complete CRM data.


For sales leaders, the time drain of their teams doing manual data entry and admin work previously created a painful trade-off: The only way to scale pipeline coverage was to hire more people. But thanks to the productivity gains and trusted context from sales agents, sales teams are able to scale efficiently, and 57% of surveyed sales leaders agree that these agents help them increase revenue without adding headcount.


##### **Agents give sellers more time to engage deeply with buyers**


The administrative capacity ceiling is real. Sales reps can spend the[majority](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/state-of-sales-report-announcement-2026/) of their workweek acting as administrative coordinators rather than actively selling. The Sales Cloud ROI report found that sales agents give sellers some of that time back:


- Almost three-quarters of customers surveyed have deployed agents across tasks like prospecting, account research, and pipeline management, and when they do, they save five hours or more per week on those tasks.
- Overall, sales agents save sellers an average of six hours per week on individual, non-selling tasks to focus on strategy and relationship building

> Reps were taking four to eight hours — or even a day — to follow up with leads. Sales Cloud helped us shorten that window and focus our team on higher-value conversations. It’s made scaling outreach a lot more manageable.
>

> David Beiler, VP, Sales, Equipter


At many companies, the buying committees have ballooned to eight to 10 people, leading to buyer paralysis and stalled negotiations. Sellers don’t always have the hours to map and build consensus across multi-stakeholder deals. But, according to the research, when they have access to sales agents, all of the customers surveyed report being able to handle more leads and accounts with agents than without.


- Two in three sales leaders spend more time on partner and channel relationships.
- Two in three sales leaders (67%) spend more time engaging wider buying committees.
- One in three spend more time on retaining the relationships post-sale.

# Image Modal


##### **Sales agents eliminate guesswork, improving context for better deal cycles**


It’s hard to build a reliable sales forecast when deals depend on reps typing up notes from memory or forgetting to do research on an account at the end of a long week. The data shows that, by logging conversations and account research automatically into Salesforce, agents give sellers the ability to see what’s actually happening in the pipeline.


- Sixty-three percent of sales agent customers report more accurate and complete CRM data.
- Two in three sales agent customers report improved account research thoroughness.


Customers using sales agents say the accuracy and visibility has led to easier deal cycles.


- Two in three sales agent customers report smoother handoffs across the revenue cycle as a result of agents.
- Deals move 10% to 20% faster for two-thirds of account executives.


##### **Headcounts remain steady while revenue increases with agents**


When they implement agents, sales leaders no longer have to grow by hiring more people.


- Fifty-seven percent of sales leaders agree that AI agents allow their business to increase revenue without adding headcount.
- Three in four sales leaders (75%) say they have kept their exact same hiring plans while actively increasing overall sales output.


##### **The verdict? Sales agents liberate salespeople and grow revenue**


AI isn’t replacing the sales rep; it’s rescuing the profession. If agents can handle the admin, sellers can spend more time with the buyer, which is what they wanted all along.


###### Read more:


- Read the full[ROI Report: Sales Cloud Agents](http://salesforce.com/sales/resources/sales-agent-roi-report)
- Discover more insights from sales teams in the[2026 State of Sales Report](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/state-of-sales/)


**Methodology:** Data comes from an online survey among 24 Sales Cloud customers between July 21 and 22, 2026, asking 32 questions about their experience with Sales Cloud agents. Respondents were drawn from two sources: existing Sales Cloud customers invited to take part directly and additional Sales Cloud users sourced through a third-party research panel. All were screened to confirm they were active users of Sales Cloud’s AI sales agents.
